name: US recession risk
summary: Sahm recession indicator 0.00 for October; yield curve +0.27 on 13 Nov; jobless claims near a one-year low
state: The real-time Sahm rule indicator was 0.00 for October, far from the 0.5 trigger (FRED). The 10y–2y Treasury curve was +0.27 on 13 Nov, up from +0.24 a day earlier. Initial jobless claims were 200,000 in the week to 7 Nov, with the four-week average of 195,250 at its lowest in a year (FRED).
for_you: The US labour market shows no recession signal. A US downturn would tend to weigh on UK exports and global markets.

sources.title: FRED — Real-time Sahm Rule Recession Indicator

why: A US recession drags world trade, earnings and jobs; it is the single biggest swing factor for the global cycle.
drivers: Labour market, consumer spending, credit conditions, rates and fiscal policy.

rubric.alert: Sahm ≥ 0.50, or two consecutive negative GDP quarters, or NBER declares recession.
rubric.watch: Sahm 0.30–0.49, or one negative GDP quarter, or payrolls negative in a release.
rubric.normal: Sahm rule indicator < 0.30 and no negative GDP quarter in the latest two releases.
